View Test Case
Preconditions
AddPassenger completed; getAddPaxOfferId/getAddPaxResponceID available. Collection variables reset before starting (SPEC.md §6.1).
Steps
  1. AddPassenger -> GetSeatMap (send ResponseId/selectedOfferId = AddPassenger's IDs) -> capture resp.offerId/resp.responseId -> Book (send ResponseId=getSeatMapResponceID, selectedOfferId=getSeatMapOfferId).
Expected Result
GetSeatMap returns HTTP 200 with a non-empty offerId/responseId; the collection variables getSeatMapOfferId and getSeatMapResponceID (note the collection's own "Responce" spelling) are populated from these; Book accepts them and returns pnr/bookingToken/gdsPNR without needing AddPassenger's IDs re-sent -- this is a behavior change from before 2026-08-10, when GetSeatMap set no variables at all and Book still read AddPassenger's IDs.
Actual Result
Half confirmed, half blocked. GetSeatMap returned non-empty offerId/responseId (both re-issued: different from AddPassenger's), and Book accepted them as its ResponseId/selectedOfferId (no ID or validation error; it ran the full supplier round-trip). It then failed at Galileo's ticketing step, so no pnr/bookingToken/gdsPNR came back. Book cannot complete for Galileo/EGY on this host. All 10 Book calls that passed request validation ended with the same HTTP 409 NDC-INT-UNC-Z9999 (host error 12008: "INVALID CREDIT CARD DETAILS the reservation failed at Ticketing stage and still at the hold state with gdsPnr ..."), after 31-51 s, and returned no pnr/bookingToken; all 3 BookAfterHold calls fail the same way (409, "Indicates FOP application failed: CHECK DATE"). This looks like an expired or invalid form-of-payment card on the EGY Galileo credentials (an environment problem, not an API defect), so no booking can be created or read back. The Postman collection-variable assignment is script-side and not observable over raw HTTP.
TC-BOOK-POS-03 - Validate Book accepts a single-passenger, single-segment passengersSelectedSeats selection and echoes it correctly.BLOCKED
Endpoint Name: Confirm a booking with one chosen seat is accepted and the seat shows in the confirmation
Request: Booked one adult on a Cairo to Jeddah flight (2026-11-20) with seat 33-E
Response: The booking was sent to the airline system, which refused to issue the ticket (invalid credit card on the account); no confirmation came back
Expected: Booking succeeds and the confirmation shows the seat, its price and the updated total
Actual: Blocked by the environment: no booking can be completed with this account until the card is fixed
Status: BLOCKED
Evidence
Book 409 in 41.8 s, gdsPnr HNC0JN; request passengersSelectedSeats key = passenger GUID from GetSeatMap passengersDetails (not "PAX1")

View Test Case
Preconditions
GetSeatMap completed; an AvailablePaid cell's cellCode and cellID recorded (TC-SEATMAP-VAL-03).
Steps
  1. AddPassenger -> GetSeatMap (record cellCode/cellID) -> Book (ResponseId=getSeatMapResponceID, selectedOfferId=getSeatMapOfferId, passengersSelectedSeats as above).
Expected Result
HTTP 200; pnr/bookingToken/gdsPNR returned; response top-level passengersSelectedSeats.T1.S1 == {cellCode:"12E", price:{amount,currency}}; selectedOffer.passengerFareBreakdown[].passengerSeats contains the same {cellCode,price}; selectedOffer.priceDetails.totalSelectedSeats/totalSelectedSeatsAmount reflect the same price.
Actual Result
Blocked. Book cannot complete for Galileo/EGY on this host. All 10 Book calls that passed request validation ended with the same HTTP 409 NDC-INT-UNC-Z9999 (host error 12008: "INVALID CREDIT CARD DETAILS the reservation failed at Ticketing stage and still at the hold state with gdsPnr ..."), after 31-51 s, and returned no pnr/bookingToken; all 3 BookAfterHold calls fail the same way (409, "Indicates FOP application failed: CHECK DATE"). This looks like an expired or invalid form-of-payment card on the EGY Galileo credentials (an environment problem, not an API defect), so no booking can be created or read back. The seat selection itself passed Book's validation (a mismatched or unavailable seat gets a 400 in 0.1 s on this supplier; this one ran the full supplier round-trip), but the response shape with the echoed seat cannot be captured. For reference only, the Hold endpoint (not Book) echoes a seat on this supplier: Hold with seat 33-H returned passengersSelectedSeats {33-H, 80 AED} and totalSelectedSeatsAmount 80 AED (see FLOW-V2-50-SEATFIELD).
TC-SEATAFTERHOLD-POS-01 - Discovery case -- submit the collection's documented 6-field body against a live Held PNR and capture the actual response shape.FAIL
Endpoint Name: Find out what the "add a seat to a held booking" call really does
Request: Held a Cairo to Dubai booking, then called the add-seat-after-hold request with the six documented fields
Response: Refused immediately: this action is "not supported" for this airline
Expected: Unknown - to be discovered
Actual: BUG-03, 11th confirmed occurrence (first on this airline) — the call is not available for Galileo, so its real behaviour is still unknown
Status: FAIL
Evidence
Hold 200 pnr 7JQQC8; SeatAfterHold 409 OperationNotSupported in 0.1s; Context OperationNotSupported = "Galileo does not exists"

View Test Case
Preconditions
Hold completed; pnr/gdsPNR/bookingToken available and not yet expired (holdExpirationDate in the future).
Steps
  1. Hold (capture pnr, gdsPNR, bookingToken, holdExpirationDate) -> SeatAfterHold (POST api/v2/SeatMap/SeatAfterHold with supplier, credentialsSelector, pnr, gdsPNR, bookingToken, surName) -> record the raw status code and full response body verbatim.
Expected Result
UNKNOWN by design -- no expected shape exists anywhere in SPEC.md or the collection (§2.7a). This case's purpose is to establish ground truth: does it return 200 with a seat-map-like payload to choose from, does it require a follow-up call, or does it error demanding fields not shown in the saved example? Record exactly what happens; do not force-fit the result into an assumed shape.
Actual Result
Ground truth: STILL REPRODUCES (BUG-03, 11th confirmed occurrence overall; first on Galileo). SeatAfterHold rejects Galileo outright at supplier level before reading any field: 409 OperationNotSupported, with the same odd wording ("Galileo does not exists") used for GulfAir and FlyAdeal. The Hold itself works (200, pnr 7JQQC8, gdsPNR HNC0JS, holdExpirationDate 2026-12-13T23:59:00+02:00), so the Held PNR the endpoint needs exists; the endpoint is simply not implemented for this supplier. The real request contract stays unknown.

View Test Case
Preconditions
AddPassenger completed; getAddPaxOfferId/getAddPaxResponceID available.
Steps
  1. AddPassenger -> GetSeatMap (send ResponseId/selectedOfferId = AddPassenger's IDs) -> inspect the raw response.
Expected Result
Automatable assertions: HTTP 200; supplier, flightSegments, passengersDetails, seatMapDetails all present and non-null; seatMapDetails has at least one key; every segmentRefId key in seatMapDetails also appears in flightSegments and in the offer's segments from FareConfirm/AddPassenger (no orphan/missing segments in either direction).
Actual Result
Confirmed. All four blocks are present and non-null. The single seatMapDetails key (nDOS+DTqWDKAxpUeTAAAAA==) appears identically in the seat map's flightSegments and in FareConfirm's flightSegments; no orphan in either direction. Capability notes: FareConfirm reports isSeatMapRequired=false (BUG-15), but the seat map works for this flight. Seat maps are carrier-dependent on Galileo: SV (A330 330/333) and MS (A320neo 32N) return maps; NE and XY return 409 (see TC-SEATMAP-NEG-05).

View Test Case
Preconditions
GetSeatMap completed; a cellCode/cellId recorded for an AvailablePaid cell; the pnr's bookingStatus/ticketStatus (per Retrieve) confirmed not yet ticketed before this check is made.
Steps
  1. AddPassenger -> GetSeatMap (record cellCode/cellId) -> Book (submit passengersSelectedSeats) -> Retrieve immediately afterward, with no ticketing action taken in between -> inspect bookingStatus/ticketStatus alongside the seat-related fields.
Expected Result
Automatable assertion: the immediate post-Book Retrieve already shows passengersSelectedSeats/passengerSeats/totalSelectedSeatsAmount populated with the selected seat, while bookingStatus/ticketStatus still reads as un-ticketed/un-issued (e.g. Booked, not Ticketed). This confirms the seat is attached to the reservation at Book time and does not depend on a later payment/ticketing step existing or completing. If bookingStatus already reads as ticketed/paid immediately post-Book with no intervening action taken, record that as a finding rather than assuming the AC's ordering holds.
Actual Result
Blocked: Book cannot complete for Galileo/EGY on this host: every Book that reaches the supplier fails at the ticketing step (invalid credit card on the credentials), so no booking is created. On the Hold path the seat is attached to the reservation immediately (visible on Retrieve before any ticketing), which suggests the same at Book time, but that is not this case.

View Test Case
Preconditions
GetSeatMap completed for a confirmed offer; a specific AvailablePaid cell identified in the response.
Steps
  1. GetSeatMap -> record cellDetails.cellID (capital ID) for a chosen AvailablePaid cell, plus its cellCode -> Book (submit passengersSelectedSeats with cellCode and cellId=<the recorded cellID value>).
Expected Result
Book accepts the token despite the field-name casing difference between the response (cellID) and the request (cellId) and attaches the correct seat, echoed back in the response's passengersSelectedSeats/selectedOffer.passengerFareBreakdown[].passengerSeats.
Actual Result
Blocked. The request itself was accepted: it carried the response's cellID verbatim under the lowercase-d name cellId and passed all seat validation (the same endpoint rejects any mismatched or unavailable seat with a 400 in 0.1 s, see TC-BOOK-NEG-06/VAL-06/NEG-05), so the casing difference is cosmetic. But the booking then failed at ticketing, so the seat echo (attached seat, price, the three echo locations) cannot be verified. Book cannot complete for Galileo/EGY on this host: every Book that reaches the supplier fails at the ticketing step (invalid credit card on the credentials), so no booking is created.
TC-SEATMAP-VAL-04 - Validate a cellID obtained from one offer's GetSeatMap response is rejected when submitted in Book for a different offer.PASS
Endpoint Name: Confirm a seat code taken from one flight offer is refused when used on a different offer
Request: Opened seat maps for two separate offers, then booked on the second offer with seat 34-F but using the seat code copied from the first offer's seat 33-H
Response: Refused at once with a clear 400 error saying the seat code does not match the seat the token identifies; no booking was created
Expected: The request should be refused
Actual: Confirmed — this airline does check the token. The earlier defect (BUG-07), where a foreign token was accepted and the seat silently dropped, did not appear
Status: PASS
Evidence
Book 400 in 0.1s; Context: Seat 'CellCode' value '34-F' does not match the seat identified by 'CellId' ('33-H'); no pnr, no gdsPnr

View Test Case
Preconditions
Two independent, completed Search->FareConfirm->AddPassenger->GetSeatMap chains (Offer A and Offer B) for the same supplier/credentialsSelector.
Steps
  1. Chain A: Search->FareConfirm->AddPassenger->GetSeatMap, record cellID_A. Chain B: Search->FareConfirm->AddPassenger->GetSeatMap, obtain getSeatMapResponceID_B/getSeatMapOfferId_B. Book using Chain B's ResponseId/selectedOfferId but passengersSelectedSeats.cellId=cellID_A.
Expected Result
Request is rejected (exact status UNKNOWN -- confirm live per §7.9), since cellID appears (per its base64-decoded contents) to embed the originating ResponseId/OfferId/passenger-ref metadata and is presumably bound to the offer it was issued for.
Actual Result
Rejected as expected, and BUG-07 did NOT reproduce. Galileo decodes the cellId, finds it names seat 33-H (the other offer's seat), compares it with the submitted cellCode 34-F and refuses the request with a specific 400 in 0.1 s, before any supplier call; no booking and no held reservation were created. This is the first supplier on which the foreign-cellId check works (GulfAir and FlyAdeal accept it and silently drop the seat). Note the check is code-vs-id consistency; whether an id of the SAME seat number from another offer is refused was not separable here (the token is just "<seat>~0B5").
TC-BOOK-VAL-06 - Validate Book's behavior when passengersSelectedSeats.cellCode does not match the cell that cellId actually encodes.PASS
Endpoint Name: Confirm what happens when the seat code and the seat token point at different seats
Request: Booked with seat code 35-F but the token of seat 33-D
Response: Refused immediately with a clear 400 error saying the two do not match; nothing was booked
Expected: Unknown - either the token wins, the code wins, or the request is refused
Actual: Resolved: this airline refuses a mismatched pair
Status: PASS
Evidence
Book 400 in 0.1s; message names both values; no pnr. Also L Book (cellCode 99-Z + cellId of 21-H): 400, same message form

View Test Case
Preconditions
GetSeatMap completed; a valid cellCode/cellId pair recorded for one cell, plus a second cellCode value from a different cell.
Steps
  1. GetSeatMap (record cellCode="12E"/cellId for that cell, and note a different cell's cellCode, e.g. "14C") -> Book (submit passengersSelectedSeats with cellCode="14C" but cellId = the "12E" token).
Expected Result
UNKNOWN -- confirm live whether the API trusts cellId alone (ignoring/overwriting the mismatched cellCode), rejects the request outright, or books the wrong seat under the wrong displayed code. All three are plausible given cellId is described as the metadata-bearing field and cellCode as a display label.
Actual Result
Resolved: Galileo rejects the mismatch outright with a specific 400 in 0.1 s and creates nothing. It does not trust one field over the other (unlike GulfAir, which trusts cellCode and ignores the cellId, BUG-06). A third case in the same family, a made-up seat code "99-Z" with a real cellId, is rejected the same way (see TC-BOOK-NEG-09 notes). Both fields must be kept in sync in every future case.

View Test Case
Preconditions
GetSeatMap completed for a confirmed offer with a populated seatMapDetails.
Steps
  1. GetSeatMap -> for every cell's cellCharacteristics[], pair padisCode with description -> check each pair against a maintained reference mapping (e.g. A=Aisle, W=Window, E=Exit seat, per the QC checklist's simplified mapping) -- note SPEC.md §2.7/§8.3 itself has observed a wider code set (CH, _8, _9, _14, K, LS, OW, RS, V, FC, Unknown) not covered by the checklist's simplified 5-code table.
Expected Result
Automatable assertion: for every padisCode value observed, description must not contradict the code's known meaning per the now-sourced canonical reference table. Codes still outside that table should be rare -- log any such pairing rather than asserting pass/fail.
Actual Result
0 contradictions. All 18 codes observed (B, CH, I, K, W, _9, A, H, E, L, LS, OW, RS, _1A, _1B, IE, O, _1W) exist in the reference table and every description means what its code means. Two non-contradicting oddities are logged: (1) the wording is not the canonical text for 10 of 18 codes (e.g. W "Window" vs "Window seat", A "Aisle" vs "Aisle seat", E "ExitRow" vs "Exit and emergency exit", K "Bulkhead" vs "Bulkhead seat", L "ExtraLegRoom" vs "Leg space seat", CH "PaidGeneralSeat" vs "Chargeable seat"), although the source comment says descriptions are computed from the shared table for every supplier; (2) the four codes that start with a digit are returned with a leading underscore (_9, _1A, _1B, _1W instead of 9, 1A, 1B, 1W). Seat cells' own description string always equals its characteristics' descriptions joined with "; " (0 exceptions).

View Test Case
Preconditions
GetSeatMap completed for a confirmed offer with at least one Aisle-category cell present.
Steps
  1. GetSeatMap -> for every cell, branch on cellCategory -> if Aisle, assert column and cellDetails; if Seat, assert column and cellDetails.
Expected Result
Automatable assertion: cellCategory=Aisle implies column is null AND cellDetails is null; cellCategory=Seat implies column is non-null AND cellDetails is a populated object (per TC-SEATMAP-REG-02's field list). No cell violates this partition.
Actual Result
0 violations. All 1263 Aisle cells have column null and cellDetails null; all 4890 Seat cells have a letter column (A, B, C, D, E, F, H, J, K, L) and a populated cellDetails object. The 392 NoSeat cells (not covered by this rule) have cellDetails null and keep their column letter.

Large arrays, objects and long opaque tokens are truncated for report length (marked "__omitted__" / "[truncated]"); the full payload was inspected live. Raw supplier payloads are redacted per SPEC.md §7.14.
View Test Case
Preconditions
GetSeatMap completed with a populated seatMapDetails covering a mix of window/aisle/middle/exit-row seats.
Steps
  1. GetSeatMap -> for every Seat-category cell, read cellCharacteristics[].padisCode -> classify each cell as window/aisle/extra-legroom/other using the reference table -> spot-check against the cell's own column position (e.g. the outermost column of a zone should carry a window-adjacent code) and description text.
Expected Result
Automatable assertion: for codes present in the now-sourced canonical reference table (NDC_Integration/Resources/SeatResources/PadisSeatCharacteristic.md), the derived classification must not contradict column position or description text. Codes outside that table are logged, not failed.
Actual Result
0 contradictions. Every one of the 4890 seats carries exactly one position marker (window W / _1W, aisle A or centre _9); all 1168 window seats are at the edge of their row, all 2372 aisle seats touch an Aisle cell, no centre seat does, and the description text always matches the codes. Exit rows (228 cells) are derivable from E; 168 of them also carry "Seat not suitable for child" and "Seat not allowed for infant/medical" (the other 60 exit cells, on the A320neo, carry no restriction flags). The new BUG-23 pattern (one code on every seat) did not appear: K (Bulkhead) appears only on 30 cells.
TC-SEATMAP-VAL-08 - Verify seatPriceDetails/seatPriceDetailsByPassenger is populated (non-null) for every AvailablePaid cell and null/absent for every Blocked or Occupied cell.FAIL

Response: All bookable seats are priced, but blocked and occupied seats are priced too
Expected: Blocked and occupied seats carry no price
Actual: BUG-20, 2nd confirmed occurrence (first on this airline) — unbuyable seats show real prices
Status: FAIL
Evidence
Blocked 121/121 priced; Occupied 3/3 priced; seatPriceDetails null: 0 of 4890; paid cells without price: 0

View Test Case
Preconditions
GetSeatMap completed with a populated seatMapDetails containing a mix of AvailablePaid, Blocked, and Occupied cells.
Steps
  1. GetSeatMap -> for every cell, read cellAvailability and cellDetails.seatPriceDetails/seatPriceDetailsByPassenger -> group by availability value.
Expected Result
Automatable assertion: every AvailablePaid cell has a non-null seatPriceDetailsByPassenger with populated totalPrice/basePrice/taxesPrice per passenger (cross-ref TC-SEATMAP-BIZ-02's reconciliation); every Blocked/Occupied cell has seatPriceDetails null (consistent with SPEC.md §2.7's observed example, which shows seatPriceDetails: null on a Blocked cell).
Actual Result
The AvailablePaid half holds (4766 of 4766). The Blocked/Occupied half fails: all 121 Blocked and all 3 Occupied cells carry a real price (e.g. Blocked 30-D: 160.00 AED per passenger, paxCellAvailability "Blocked") in seatPriceDetailsByPassenger, and the aggregate seatPriceDetails is populated on every cell (none is null, unlike FlyAdeal where only the aggregate was null). A client that shows prices from these fields would offer a price for seats that cannot be bought. This is BUG-20, 2nd confirmed occurrence overall (first on Galileo after FlyAdeal in Round 21).
TC-SEATMAP-VAL-09 - Verify cellCode is unique across all cells within one flight segment's seatMapDetails.PASS
Endpoint Name: Confirm no two seats on a flight share the same code
Request: Checked every seat code on 19 flights
Response: No code repeats
Expected: Each seat code appears once per flight
Actual: Confirmed — all unique
Status: PASS
Evidence
segments checked 19; segments with a duplicate cellCode: 0

View Test Case
Preconditions
GetSeatMap completed for a confirmed offer.
Steps
  1. GetSeatMap -> collect every cellCode value within one segmentRefId's rows[].cells[] -> check for duplicates.
Expected Result
Automatable assertion: no cellCode value repeats within the same segment. A duplicate seat code is a confirmed defect (SeatMap QC Execution Checklist.md §9's "Duplicate seat code" possible-bug), not an UNKNOWN.
Actual Result
No duplicates: every segment lists each seat code once (4890 codes over 19 segments, rows 21-70 depending on equipment). 0 segments with a duplicate code.
TC-SEATMAP-VAL-10 - Verify structural uniqueness and domain constraints across decks/zones/rows/columns: rowNumber unique within a segment, zoneId unique within a deck, column values restricted to {A,B,C,D,E,F,null}.PASS
Endpoint Name: Confirm rows and zones are unique and seat columns use valid letters
Request: Checked the structure of 19 flight seat layouts
Response: No row or zone repeats and aisles have no column; wide-body planes use extra column letters (H, J, K, L) beyond A to F
Expected: Unique rows and zones; columns A to F only
Actual: Confirmed — the A-to-F limit in the test is too narrow for wide-body planes (a test update, not a defect)
Status: PASS
Evidence
row duplicates 0; zone duplicates 0; rows without a declared zone 0; seat columns observed ABCDEFHJKL

View Test Case
Preconditions
GetSeatMap completed for a confirmed offer with a populated seatMapDetails.
Steps
  1. GetSeatMap -> for one segment, collect every rowNumber (check uniqueness), every zoneId per deck (check uniqueness within that deck), and every cell's column value (check domain membership).
Expected Result
Automatable assertion: no rowNumber repeats within the segment; no zoneId repeats within the same deck; every non-null column value is one of A/B/C/D/E/F (per the observed 6-column-per-row layout, SPEC.md §2.7); null column values correspond only to Aisle-category cells (cross-ref TC-SEATMAP-VAL-06).
Actual Result
Three of four constraints hold exactly: no row number repeats (19 segments), one zone per deck with no repeat, and a null column appears only on Aisle cells (1263; the 392 NoSeat cells keep a column). The fourth is flagged, not failed: the column domain. Galileo's wide-body A330 maps use A, C, D, E, F, H, J, L and some A320neo layouts B/K as well, so letters outside A-F appear (H, J, K, L; G and I are skipped, the usual airline convention). The A-F domain in this case comes from a 6-abreast sample and is too narrow; this is a test-specification update, not an API defect.

View Test Case
Preconditions
GetSeatMap completed for a multi-passenger, multi-segment offer with a populated passengersSeatMapAvailability block.
Steps
  1. GetSeatMap -> for every passenger, read passengersSeatMapAvailability.<paxRef> -> confirm every key is a segmentRefId that also appears in flightSegments/seatMapDetails using EXACTLY the same casing -> for a sample of cellCode values in each passenger's allow-list, confirm that cell's seatPriceDetailsByPassenger (if priced) includes that passenger when the passenger is expected to be priced there.
Expected Result
Automatable assertions: (1) every segmentRefId key under passengersSeatMapAvailability.<paxRef> matches the casing used elsewhere in the same response (flightSegments/seatMapDetails keys) -- a differently-cased key for the same logical segment (e.g. "Seg3" vs "SEG1"/"SEG2") is a confirmed defect, not an acceptable variation; (2) every cellCode listed in a passenger's allow-list corresponds to a real cell in that segment's seatMapDetails.
Actual Result
Both assertions hold. The allow-list is nested per passenger (passengersDetails.<paxRef>.passengersSeatMapAvailability.<segmentRefId>.<deck> = [codes]) rather than a top-level block (documentation drift, see REG-02), its segment key equals the seatMapDetails/flightSegments key exactly, every listed code exists as a cell in that segment, and every listed code is an AvailablePaid cell (Blocked/Occupied are excluded; the infant's list is empty).

View Test Case
Preconditions
GetSeatMap completed for a confirmed offer with a populated seatMapDetails.
Steps
  1. GetSeatMap -> enumerate every cells[] entry across all rows for one segment -> record the distinct cellCategory and cellAvailability/paxCellAvailability values observed.
Expected Result
Every cellCategory value observed is one of {Seat, Aisle}; every cellAvailability/paxCellAvailability value observed is one of {AvailablePaid, Blocked, Occupied}. If a new value appears (e.g. an "available free" state), log it and flag rather than hard-failing (§8.3 policy for UNKNOWN enumerations) -- do not assume the three known values are exhaustive.
Actual Result
All three expected availability values appear, and nothing else (AvailablePaid 4766, Blocked 121, Occupied 3; no AvailableFree). All 1263 Aisle cells have cellDetails null, so none carries a price. One value outside the expected set is flagged, not failed (8.3 policy): cellCategory "NoSeat" on 392 cells (cellDetails null; a taken or absent seat position, already known from GulfAir). Occupied is rare on Galileo (3 cells), Blocked common (121).

Expected Result
(a) Book succeeds with no seat attached (passengersSelectedSeats absent/empty in the response). (b) succeeds as in TC-BOOK-POS-03. (c) UNKNOWN -- confirm live whether multiple passengers/segments nest correctly as sibling keys per SPEC.md §2.9's schema description, since only the single-passenger/single-segment shape has a directly-observed example.
Actual Result
Blocked: none of the three variants can complete (Book cannot complete for Galileo/EGY on this host: every Book that reaches the supplier fails at the ticketing step (invalid credit card on the credentials), so no booking is created). What could be established: all three request shapes, including the 2-passenger x 2-segment nesting in (c) (2 passenger keys, each with 2 segment keys), passed Book's request validation and reached the supplier, so the nesting is at least accepted by the API's validation. Whether the 4 seats are attached and echoed, and whether a two-journey Book returns a pnr (BUG-21 on FlyAdeal), is unknown.

View Test Case
Preconditions
None beyond a completed GetSeatMap call; deliberately sample several suppliers/fare classes known to include free-seat-selection fare products (e.g. Ultimate/Premium bundle tiers per §2.4's bundle rule descriptions mentioning free seat rows).
Steps
  1. GetSeatMap across several suppliers/offers, prioritizing fare classes whose priceClasses.rulesAndPenalties mention seat-related perks (e.g. §2.4's observed "Seat: row 8 onwards" / "Seat: Row 3 onwards" bundle rules) -> scan every cell's cellAvailability/paxCellAvailability value -> assert AvailableFree cells have seatPriceDetails/seatPriceDetailsByPassenger null (matching the confirmed example), and continue sampling specifically for AvailableAfterReservation.
Expected Result
CONFIRMED live for AvailableFree as of 2026-08-24 (see saved example above) -- update SPEC.md §2.7/§8.3's enum list to add AvailableFree to the observed set. AvailableAfterReservation remains UNKNOWN; if found, add with evidence, if never observed after a reasonably broad sample, record it as an unconfirmed QC-checklist-only candidate rather than promoting it.
Actual Result
Not observable on this supplier. Galileo's maps contain only AvailablePaid, Blocked and Occupied (every bookable seat is a paid seat on the public fares sampled; no bundle or fare class with free seat selection exists because Galileo has no bundles), so neither value appears and this supplier cannot confirm them. AvailableFree stays confirmed from GulfAir (Round 20, passenger level) and FlyAdeal (Round 21, cell level); AvailableAfterReservation remains unconfirmed after 4890 more seat cells.

View Test Case
Preconditions
A broad sample of GetSeatMap responses across suppliers/aircraft types (widebody aircraft with galleys/bulkheads/stairs-to-upper-deck are the most likely candidates for the rarer members).
Steps
  1. GetSeatMap across several suppliers/aircraft (prioritize widebody/double-decker equipment) -> scan every cells[].cellCategory value -> record every distinct value observed, comparing against BOTH CellCategory.md's enum names and the raw example's own comment naming.
Expected Result
UNKNOWN -- resolve empirically. Only Seat and Aisle are confirmed as of 2026-08-24; every other member (including whichever name -- Lavatory or Bathroom -- the bathroom-equivalent category actually uses live) remains unconfirmed. Do not assume Seat/Aisle are exhaustive, and do not assume the C# enum's member names match what the API actually serializes (the Lavatory-vs-Bathroom naming discrepancy between the raw example's comment and the enum source must be resolved live, not guessed).
Actual Result
Resolved for this supplier, including wide-body equipment: only Seat, Aisle and NoSeat are ever returned (NoSeat on 392 cells: a taken or absent seat position with cellDetails null, matching CellCategory.md's NoSeat member). Galley, lavatory/bathroom, bulkhead, closet, door, exit-row and stairs categories do not exist on Galileo even on the A330: they are not drawn as cells at all, and exit rows / bulkhead / extra legroom are expressed through cellCharacteristics (E, K, L) instead. The Lavatory-vs-Bathroom naming question therefore stays open for any supplier.

View Test Case
Preconditions
TC-BOOK-POS-03 completed and its response captured; the same offer's pre-seat FareConfirm/AddPassenger-era totalAmount also captured.
Steps
  1. Book (with passengersSelectedSeats populated) -> read selectedOffer.priceDetails.{totalAmount, totalBaseAmount, totalTaxAmount, totalAncillariesAmount, totalSelectedSeatsAmount} -> compare totalAmount against totalBaseAmount + totalTaxAmount + totalAncillariesAmount + totalSelectedSeatsAmount, and against the pre-seat-selection totalAmount plus the seat's price.
Expected Result
UNKNOWN -- confirm live. Expected (per the existing price-reconciliation formula's pattern, §2.1) is totalAmount == totalBaseAmount + totalTaxAmount + totalAncillariesAmount + totalSelectedSeatsAmount, and totalAmount(after) == totalAmount(before seat selection) + totalSelectedSeatsAmount. Neither V1 nor V2's existing price-reconciliation test scripts were observed summing a seat amount, so this is unverified either way -- treat any mismatch as a confirmed defect, not an UNKNOWN to shrug off, once run.
Actual Result
Blocked for Book. Book cannot complete for Galileo/EGY on this host: every Book that reaches the supplier fails at the ticketing step (invalid credit card on the credentials), so no booking is created, so Book's priceDetails cannot be read. The same arithmetic was checked on the Hold path (the only path that returns a priced seat): 240 AED + 330 AED + 0 AED + 80 AED = 650 AED, and 570 AED (FareConfirm) + 80 AED = 650 AED; the seat amount is included in totalAmount there. This is supporting evidence only, not a pass for Book.
TC-BOOK-BIZ-05 - Validate a Child (CHD) passenger assigned an Exit Row seat is rejected server-side.FAIL
Endpoint Name: Confirm a child cannot be given an emergency-exit seat
Request: Booked an adult in seat 33-J and a child in exit-row seat 31-A on a Cairo to Jeddah flight
Response: The seat map offers exit-row seats to the child (even though each is labelled "not suitable for child") and the booking accepted the assignment, failing only later at the ticketing step
Expected: The booking should be refused
Actual: BUG-09, 12th confirmed occurrence (first on this airline) — the child-in-exit-row rule is not enforced
Status: FAIL
Evidence
CHD allow-list contains 12/12 exit cells, 12 of them labelled "Seat not suitable for child"; Book 409 after 51.2 s (not a 0.1 s 400); gdsPnr HNC0JV

View Test Case
Preconditions
AddPassenger completed with at least one CHD passenger; GetSeatMap completed and an exit-row cell (cellCharacteristics containing an Exit-seat characteristic) identified for that passenger's segment.
Steps
  1. AddPassenger (CHD present) -> GetSeatMap (identify an exit-row cellCode/cellId via cellCharacteristics) -> Book (assign that cellCode/cellId to the CHD passenger's setSegmentsSeats entry, bypassing any client-side UI restriction).
Expected Result
Automatable assertion: response status is an error (candidate error code RESTRICTED_EXIT_ROW_SEAT_FOR_CHILD, per this suite's Seat map - Seatmap.md TC-INT-BOOK-008 reference) and no pnr is created for this attempt. Candidate code is UNKNOWN-confirm-live -- not yet observed in any Postman-collection saved example; record the exact code/status returned and update this row plus SPEC.md §2.9 once confirmed.
Actual Result
STILL REPRODUCES (BUG-09, 12th confirmed occurrence overall; first on Galileo). GetSeatMap lists all 12 exit-row cells (31-A... and 53-A...) in the CHD passenger's allow-list and prices them, although every one of those cells is itself described "Seat not suitable for child" (padis IE). Book then accepts the assignment: instead of a 0.1 s validation 400 (what the same endpoint returns for an unavailable or mismatched seat), it ran the full supplier call for 51.2 s and failed only at the unrelated ticketing step. The booking therefore reached Galileo with a child in an exit row; whether the seat stayed on the held reservation (HNC0JV) cannot be read back. The safety rule is not enforced by the API.
TC-BOOK-BIZ-06 - Verify an Infant (INF) passenger travelling on an Adult's lap is not charged a seat fee and requires no passengersSelectedSeats entry.BLOCKED
Endpoint Name: Confirm an infant on an adult's lap is not charged for a seat and needs no seat entry
Request: Booked one adult with seat 33-L and one infant with no seat entry
Response: The request was accepted by the checks and sent to the airline system, which refused to issue the ticket (invalid credit card); the seat map lists the infant with no seats and no prices
Expected: Booking succeeds, no seat fee for the infant, totals count only the adult seat
Actual: Blocked by the environment: no booking can be completed
Status: BLOCKED
Evidence
Book 409 after 49.1 s (gdsPnr HNC0K3); INF allow-list length 0; INF price entries on all cells 0

View Test Case
Preconditions
AddPassenger completed with one ADT + one INF (parentPaxRefId linking them, §2.5); GetSeatMap completed; a seat selected only for the ADT.
Steps
  1. AddPassenger (ADT+INF) -> GetSeatMap -> Book (passengersSelectedSeats contains only the ADT's paxRef; INF's paxRef is absent from passengersSelectedSeats entirely) -> Retrieve.
Expected Result
Automatable assertions: Book/Retrieve succeed; selectedOffer.passengerFareBreakdown for the INF paxRef has paxTotalSeatAmount.amount == 0 (or the field/array absent) and no passengerSeats entries; the ADT's paxTotalSeatAmount matches the selected cell's price; totalSelectedSeatsAmount equals only the ADT's seat price, not double-counted for the INF.
Actual Result
Blocked: no booking can be completed, so the response and Retrieve assertions cannot be checked (Book cannot complete for Galileo/EGY on this host: every Book that reaches the supplier fails at the ticketing step (invalid credit card on the credentials), so no booking is created). What was established: the ADT-only seat request with no INF entry passed Book's request validation (it reached the supplier, no 400). The seat map also treats the infant correctly: the INF is listed in passengersDetails with an empty allow-list (0 seats) and has no seatPriceDetailsByPassenger entry on any cell.

View Test Case
Preconditions
AddPassenger completed; GetSeatMap completed and a wheelchair-accessible cell identified by inspecting cellCharacteristics/description text.
Steps
  1. GetSeatMap (identify a wheelchair-accessible cell by description/characteristics) -> Book (assign that cell to the relevant passenger) -> Retrieve.
Expected Result
UNKNOWN -- confirm live. Expect Book/Retrieve to succeed with the seat attached like any other paid/free seat; there is no evidenced SSR (special-service-request) field anywhere in the current V2 Book/AddPassenger schema (§2.5/§2.9) to carry a WCHR code alongside the seat, so if Seat map - Seatmap.md's TC-INT-BOOK-014 expectation of a linked SSR flag is correct, that would be an undocumented field this suite has not yet discovered -- treat any SSR-linkage behavior found as a new SPEC.md §2.9 finding, not something to assume exists.
Actual Result
Blocked at the Book step (Book cannot complete for Galileo/EGY on this host: every Book that reaches the supplier fails at the ticketing step (invalid credit card on the credentials), so no booking is created). Unlike GulfAir and FlyAdeal, whose seat vocabularies have no wheelchair marker, Galileo does expose one: padisCode H "Handicapped" on 110 cells, so a suitable cell can be identified; the part that cannot be done is booking it and reading the assignment back. The V2 AddPassenger/Book schema still has no special-assistance field to carry a WCHR code alongside the seat.

GetSeatMap completed for a multi-passenger offer with a populated seatMapDetails.

GetSeatMap -> for a sample of cells, compare cellAvailability (overall) against the set of passenger refs actually present in seatPriceDetailsByPassenger for that cell -> cross-check each listed passenger's presence against passengersSeatMapAvailability.<paxRef>.<segmentRefId> (the separate top-level per-passenger cellCode allow-list, also confirmed present in the same saved example).
Expected Result
Automatable assertion (structural, not value-equality, and NOT a completeness requirement): a passenger's absence from a cell's seatPriceDetailsByPassenger is EXPECTED and valid whenever that passenger is not eligible for that cell (confirmed pattern: a CHD/INF passenger restricted from a forward/exit cell won't appear there, per this same example's passengersSeatMapAvailability showing PAX3/PAX4 with a much shorter or empty allow-list than PAX1/PAX2). Do NOT assert every passenger must appear per priced cell -- only assert internal consistency: a passenger listed in seatPriceDetailsByPassenger for a cell SHOULD also have that cell's cellCode present in their own passengersSeatMapAvailability entry (if that top-level structure is present in the response). Do not assert cellAvailability == a per-passenger equivalent for all passengers either, since SeatMap QC Execution Checklist.md §11 explicitly notes these may differ legitimately (e.g. a seat blocked for one passenger type but not another).
Actual Result
Consistent for every bookable seat (all 6371 allow-listed entries are priced, every allow-listed code exists as a cell, paxCellAvailability always equals the cell's cellAvailability, and the infant is correctly absent from every cell with an empty allow-list: 0 entries, 0 allowed). It fails the other direction: 157 priced entries exist for Blocked/Occupied cells the passenger is not allowed to select (the allow-list excludes them), i.e. the price list still advertises seats that cannot be bought - the same defect as TC-SEATMAP-VAL-08 (BUG-20).

Preconditions
A test environment/mechanism that can independently occupy a seat between the two GetSeatMap calls (may require a second tester/session or coordination with the team -- environment-dependent, same caveat class as TC-BOOK-NEG-09).
Steps
  1. GetSeatMap call #1 (record a specific cell's cellAvailability) -> independently occupy/select that same cell via a separate booking action -> GetSeatMap call #2 (same offer/segment) -> compare the cell's cellAvailability between the two calls.
Expected Result
UNKNOWN -- resolve empirically; if reliably forceable, expect the cell's cellAvailability to transition (e.g. AvailablePaid -> Occupied) between the two calls, confirming a live supplier round-trip rather than a cached response. If not reliably forceable in this environment, downgrade to logging response timing/headers (e.g. absence of a Cache-Control/ETag suggesting no caching layer) as weaker circumstantial evidence instead.
Actual Result
CONFIRMED live inventory (as for GulfAir and FlyAdeal). The seat taken by this session's own held reservation (pnr 7JRHGS) turned Occupied on the very next seat map, both on the same offer and on a completely fresh offer for the same flight. The seat map is read live from the supplier, not cached; a Hold (not only a ticketed booking) is enough to take the seat.

View Test Case
Preconditions
GetSeatMap completed for a confirmed offer.
Steps
  1. GetSeatMap -> snapshot the full response -> schema-diff against SPEC.md §2.7's current field list -> explicitly branch on which cabinLayoutsByDeck shape this supplier returns (zones[].{zoneId,columns} vs. a flat columns[] array) and whether rows[] entries carry zoneId at all, rather than assuming one shape.
Expected Result
Every OTHER key listed in SPEC.md §2.7 (rows[].{rowNumber,deck,cells[].{cellCategory,column,cellDetails.{cellID,cellCode,cellAvailability,name,description,seatPriceDetails,seatPriceDetailsByPassenger,cellCharacteristics}}}) is present and correctly typed. The cabinLayoutsByDeck/zoneId shape is now confirmed to vary by supplier -- do NOT hard-fail a response for lacking zones[]/zoneId if it instead provides the flat columns[] array (AirArabia-confirmed variant); do NOT hard-fail a response for lacking the flat columns[] array if it instead provides zones[]/zoneId. Treat presence of at least one of the two shapes as passing, and log which shape each supplier uses.
Actual Result
Every documented key is present and correctly typed (zones[]/zoneId layout on all 19 segments; every row carries a zoneId declared in its deck; cellDetails complete with cellID/cellCode/cellAvailability/name/description/seatPriceDetails/seatPriceDetailsByPassenger/cellCharacteristics). The response also carries fields SPEC.md 2.7 does not list: top-level offerId, responseId, isFareCheckRequired, and passengersDetails.<paxRef>.{birthDate, documentNumber, passengersSeatMapAvailability}, plus the NoSeat cell category. Same schema drift flagged in every prior round, so kept FAIL for continuity; nothing is missing or mistyped. Layout variant for the supplier log: Galileo uses zones[] (not the flat columns[] variant).

Preconditions
TC-BOOK-POS-03 completed and its response available.
Steps
  1. Book (one seat, one passenger) -> read selectedOffer.passengerFareBreakdown[<that pax>].passengerSeats[0].price.amount -> read the same entry's paxTotalSeatAmount.amount -> compare.
Expected Result
Automatable assertion: the two amounts are exactly equal (and same currency). This directly encodes the schema-discrepancy defect pattern flagged in Seat map - Seatmap.md TC-INT-BOOK-005 (its own example shows a hypothetical 50.0-vs-100.0 mismatch) -- any observed mismatch is a confirmed defect against §2.9's response schema, not an UNKNOWN.
Actual Result
Blocked for Book (Book cannot complete for Galileo/EGY on this host: every Book that reaches the supplier fails at the ticketing step (invalid credit card on the credentials), so no booking is created). On the only path that returns both fields (Retrieve of the held reservation) they agree: 80 AED == 80 AED. Hold and PnrReprice responses carry neither field (see BUG-18 on FLOW-V2-50-SEATFIELD). Supporting evidence only.

Steps
  1. Book (seat selected) -> Retrieve #1 (record passengersSelectedSeats/passengerSeats/totalSelectedSeats) -> wait for ticketing to complete (tickets[].ticketStatus transitions, ticketingDate populated) -> Retrieve #2 -> compare seat-related fields between #1 and #2.
Expected Result

Actual Result
Blocked: the booked-to-ticketed transition never happens on this host (invalid credit card on the Galileo credentials), so there is no "after issue" Retrieve to compare. The Hold-path Retrieve itself works and shows the seat (33-H) on the OnHold booking.

View Test Case
Preconditions
GetSeatMap completed; at least one Blocked or Occupied cell identified in the response.
Steps
  1. GetSeatMap (identify a Blocked/Occupied cell) -> Book (submit passengersSelectedSeats using that cell's cellCode/cellId).
Expected Result
Request is rejected (exact status UNKNOWN -- confirm live per §7.9); no booking is created, or if a PNR is created it must NOT reflect the unavailable seat as attached -- either outcome should be logged precisely, since both are plausible failure modes for an unenforced availability check.
Actual Result
Rejected cleanly and quickly (0.1 s, before any supplier call) with a specific, on-point message, and no booking or held reservation was created. The blocked cell is refused even though its seat-map entry shows a price (160 AED, see BUG-20) - Book trusts the passenger allow-list, which correctly excludes it (blocked seats are absent from the passenger's allow-list). Occupied seats were not targeted separately (only 3 Occupied cells existed in the round).

View Test Case
Preconditions
GetSeatMap completed; a valid cellID recorded.
Steps
  1. GetSeatMap (record a valid cellID) -> Book (submit passengersSelectedSeats with cellId = the same token minus its last ~10 characters, or with one character flipped).
Expected Result
Request is rejected (exact status UNKNOWN -- confirm live) since the tampered token should fail whatever server-side decode/signature check the opaque cellId undergoes.
Actual Result
Rejected with a structured 400 in 0.1 s and no booking created (BUG-06, where GulfAir accepted a tampered cellId, did NOT reproduce on Galileo). The token here is short (8 characters), so "the last ~10 characters" was applied as: last 4 replaced with XXXX. The server reads the token as a seat reference and compares it with cellCode, so the tamper is caught as a code/id mismatch rather than by a signature check.

SeatAfterHold also rejects Galileo outright (BUG-03), so the expired-hold behaviour would not be visible anyway.

View Test Case
Preconditions
AddPassenger completed with 2+ passengers; GetSeatMap completed and one AvailablePaid cellCode/cellId recorded.
Steps
  1. AddPassenger -> GetSeatMap (record one cellCode/cellId) -> Book (submit passengersSelectedSeats.T1.setSegmentsSeats.<seg>=that cell AND passengersSelectedSeats.T2.setSegmentsSeats.<seg>=the same cell).
Expected Result
Automatable assertion: request rejected (candidate error code DUPLICATE_SEAT_SELECTION_IN_REQUEST, per Seat map - Seatmap.md TC-INT-BOOK-009) before any supplier round-trip; exact status UNKNOWN-confirm-live. No pnr created.
Actual Result
Rejected cleanly and fast (0.1 s, so before any supplier call) with a specific, on-point validation message naming the seat and the segment; no booking or held reservation was created. The candidate error code DUPLICATE_SEAT_SELECTION_IN_REQUEST is not used: the real shape is the generic NDC-INT-TEC-A0001 with the explanation in Context[].Value (FlyAdeal additionally returned a PredicateValidator entry).
TC-BOOK-NEG-08 - Validate Book rejects a request where the same passenger selects two different seats on the same segment.PASS
Endpoint Name: Document what happens when the same flight appears twice under one passenger in the seat request
Request: Sent two raw requests where one passenger has two entries for the same flight (a client cannot normally do this)
Response: No error for the duplicate itself; the server uses the last entry and ignores the first
Expected: Unknown - to document the behaviour
Actual: Confirmed — last entry wins, silently (same as the other airlines)
Status: PASS
Evidence
run 1 409 (gdsPnr HNC0JY); run 2 400 names 99-Z only
Attempt 1 of 2 - 33-F then 34-C (both valid)

View Test Case
Preconditions
AddPassenger completed; GetSeatMap completed with 2+ AvailablePaid cells recorded for the same segment.
Steps
  1. AddPassenger -> GetSeatMap (record two distinct cellCode/cellId pairs for the same segmentRefId) -> Book (attempt to submit both under the same passengersSelectedSeats.<pax>.setSegmentsSeats.<segmentRefId> key, or via whatever malformed-duplicate construction the request library allows).
Expected Result
UNKNOWN -- since setSegmentsSeats is keyed by segmentRefId (a JSON object, not an array), a client cannot literally submit two values under one key -- this case instead documents that constraint and verifies the last-value-wins/serialization behavior of the test client is understood, rather than asserting a specific API rejection.
Actual Result
Constraint documented and behaviour observed: in valid JSON a segment key can appear only once, and when a raw body forces the duplicate the server keeps the LAST value and discards the first without any error (run 2: only the second entry, 99-Z, is validated and named in the error; the valid first entry 33-F is never mentioned). Run 1 (two valid seats) was accepted by validation and failed only at ticketing, so the booking-level outcome (34-C attached) cannot be read back, but run 2 proves which value wins. Same as GulfAir (Round 20) and FlyAdeal (Round 21).
TC-BOOK-NEG-09 - Validate graceful rollback (no orphaned PNR or charge) when the supplier's seat allocation call fails or times out after Book is submitted with a seat selection.FAIL
Endpoint Name: Confirm a failure at the airline after booking leaves no orphan booking or charge
Request: Booked a seat on a Cairo to Jeddah flight; the airline system failed at the ticket-issue step (invalid credit card), which is a real airline-side failure after the booking was accepted
Response: The API returned a generic error with no booking reference, but the airline system kept a held reservation that nobody can find or cancel through the API; this happened on every failed booking (10 of 10)
Expected: An error and a clean rollback (no orphan booking)
Actual: New defect BUG-24 — failed bookings leave untraceable held reservations behind
Status: FAIL
Evidence
10 Book calls -> 10 409 responses, each naming a distinct held gdsPnr (HNC0JP, HNC0JN, HNC0JQ, HNC0JV, HNC0JY, HNC0K0, HNC0K1, HNC0K2, HNC0K3, HNC0K4); none returns pnr or bookingToken; error body fields: Status, TransactionId, ErrorCode, ErrorMessage, Context, OriginalSupplierRequest, OriginalSupplierResponse

View Test Case
Preconditions
AddPassenger and GetSeatMap completed; a mechanism to force or simulate a supplier-side seat-allocation failure is available (environment-dependent -- may require coordination with the team per Seat map - Seatmap.md TC-INT-BOOK-012, since this cannot be reliably forced from the request alone in every environment).
Steps
  1. Book (with passengersSelectedSeats populated, targeting a scenario expected to fail at the supplier's seat-allocation step) -> observe status code -> Retrieve using any pnr/bookingToken echoed in the failure response (if any) to confirm no live booking was silently created with an unpriced/unassigned seat.
Expected Result
Automatable assertion (once a forcing mechanism exists): response is an error (candidate HTTP 422/502 per Seat map - Seatmap.md TC-INT-BOOK-012); either no pnr is returned, or if one is returned, a follow-up Retrieve shows the booking exists without the failed seat attached and without a seat fee charged. Exact behavior UNKNOWN -- confirm live and record; this is an environment-dependent exploratory case, not guaranteed reproducible on demand.
Actual Result
Executed on a real supplier-side failure (not the seat-allocation failure the case names, but the same property: the supplier rejects a step after Book was accepted). Result: the API returns a generic 409 with no pnr/bookingToken, but the supplier reservation is NOT rolled back - Galileo keeps a live held PNR (HNC0JN) that the caller can neither retrieve (no pnr/bookingToken) nor cancel, and the only handle is a gdsPnr buried in the free-text error message. Every one of the 10 failed Books left such an orphan (HNC0JP, HNC0JN, HNC0JQ, HNC0JV, HNC0JY, HNC0K0, HNC0K1, HNC0K2, HNC0K3, HNC0K4). This violates "no orphaned booking" and is filed as new defect BUG-24 (related to BUG-16/BUG-12, where Book errors hid a created booking). The cause here (invalid card) is environmental; the missing rollback and the missing identifiers in the error are not.
TC-BOOK-NEG-10 - Validate Book succeeds when passengersSelectedSeats is explicitly sent as an empty object ({}) rather than omitted.BLOCKED
Endpoint Name: Confirm booking copes with an explicitly empty seat selection
Request: Booked one adult with the seat selection present but empty
Response: The empty selection was accepted by the checks and sent to the airline system, which refused to issue the ticket (invalid credit card)
Expected: Booking succeeds with no seat and no seat fee
Actual: Blocked by the environment (the empty selection itself causes no error)
Status: BLOCKED
Evidence
Book 409 after 31.9 s (gdsPnr HNC0K1); no validation error

AddPassenger completed; standard no-enrichment Book preconditions.

  1. AddPassenger -> Book (submit passengersSelectedSeats: {} explicitly, all other fields as a normal no-seat Book call) -> Retrieve.
Expected Result
Automatable assertion: Book succeeds (HTTP 200), no seat fee is charged (totalSelectedSeatsAmount == 0 or absent), passengersSelectedSeats in the response is empty/absent, and no 500-level error occurs from the explicit-empty-object shape (distinct from simply omitting the field, which TC-BOOK-BND-03 run (a) already covers).
Actual Result
Blocked: the success half cannot be shown (Book cannot complete for Galileo/EGY on this host: every Book that reaches the supplier fails at the ticketing step (invalid credit card on the credentials), so no booking is created). The shape half is answered: the explicit empty object passed request validation and reached the supplier (no 400, no 500), so it is not mishandled as a bad request.

View Test Case
Preconditions
AddPassenger completed; standard Book preconditions.
Steps
  1. AddPassenger -> Book (submit passengersSelectedSeats.T1.setSegmentsSeats: {}) -> Retrieve.
Expected Result
Automatable assertion: Book succeeds; no seat is attached for T1; no error is thrown by the presence of an otherwise-empty nested object.
Actual Result
Blocked: the success half cannot be shown (Book cannot complete for Galileo/EGY on this host: every Book that reaches the supplier fails at the ticketing step (invalid credit card on the credentials), so no booking is created). Two findings: with the real passenger key (the GUID from the seat map's passengersDetails) the empty setSegmentsSeats passes validation and reaches the supplier; and the key must be that GUID, not the collection's "Pax1"/"PAX1" - an unknown key is a clean 400, so every future seat case on Galileo must read the passenger key from GetSeatMap.

omit ResponseId 409 (ticketing, gdsPnr HNC0K0) | omit selectedOfferId 400 | omit supplier 400 | omit credentialsSelector 400

Preconditions

Steps
  1. Run 1: omit ResponseId. Run 2: omit selectedOfferId. Run 3: omit supplier. Run 4: omit credentialsSelector. Each run otherwise identical to the baseline, one fresh offer per run to avoid cross-run interference.
Expected Result
Automatable assertion: all four runs are rejected (exact status UNKNOWN -- confirm live per §7.9); no pnr created in any run. Record the actual status/error shape once observed so this becomes a deterministic assertion for future automation.
Actual Result
STILL REPRODUCES (BUG-05, 11th confirmed occurrence overall; first on Galileo): omitting ResponseId is not rejected - Book ran the full supplier round-trip (30.7 s) and created a held reservation (HNC0K0) before failing at ticketing, so ResponseId is not actually required. The other three omissions are cleanly rejected with a 400 in 0.1 s (supplier and credentialsSelector with the 1001 validation envelope; selectedOfferId with a clean NDC-INT-TEC-A0001 message, so BUG-22 - the HTTP 500 seen on FlyAdeal - did NOT reproduce).

View Test Case
Preconditions
A completed FareConfirm/AddPassenger chain for an offer confirmed (via the live capability flag, §2.2) to have isSeatMapRequired=false.
Steps
  1. FareConfirm/AddPassenger (confirm isSeatMapRequired=false on the live offer) -> GetSeatMap (call anyway, using that offer's IDs) -> observe response.
Expected Result
Automatable assertion once observed: rejected or an explicit unsupported-operation envelope is returned (candidate shape: the same {ErrorCode:'OperationNotSupported', ErrorMessage:...} envelope already confirmed live for GetOfferBundles on a haveBundles=false offer, §2.4) rather than a 200 with an empty/malformed seatMapDetails. Exact shape UNKNOWN for this specific endpoint -- confirm live and record.
Actual Result
STILL REPRODUCES (BUG-15, 11th confirmed occurrence overall; first on Galileo). The capability flag says no seat map is required/offered (isSeatMapRequired false and offerHasSeat false on all 41 FareConfirm responses this round), yet GetSeatMap returns HTTP 200 with a complete seat map. The flag does not describe the real capability: it is false for SV and MS flights that have working maps and also for NE/NP/XY flights that return 409.
TC-SEATMAP-NEG-02 - Validate GetSeatMap is rejected when the request otherwise targets a valid offer but no segment of that offer's itinerary is being queried (i.e., the offer/response pair does not correspond to any real segment).FAIL
Endpoint Name: Confirm the seat map is refused when the two references come from different offers
Request: Mixed the references of two real offers, in both orders
Response: Both mixed requests returned a full seat map (always the one the offer reference points to)
Expected: Both refused
Actual: BUG-01, 11th confirmed occurrence (first on this airline) — the pair is never cross-checked
Status: FAIL
Evidence
run 1 200 (selectedOfferId of B -> SV386 CAI-JED 2026-12-21); run 2 200 (selectedOfferId of A -> MS673 CAI-JED 2026-12-20)
Attempt 1 of 2 - ResponseId of A + selectedOfferId of B

View Test Case
Preconditions
Two independent completed AddPassenger chains for two different itineraries (Offer A, Offer B).
Steps
  1. AddPassenger for Offer A and Offer B separately -> GetSeatMap using Offer A's ResponseId but Offer B's selectedOfferId (or vice versa) -> observe response.
Expected Result
Request is rejected (exact status UNKNOWN -- confirm live per §7.9); no seatMapDetails should be returned for a segment set that doesn't belong to the referenced offer.
Actual Result
STILL REPRODUCES (BUG-01, 11th confirmed occurrence overall; first on Galileo). Both mismatched pairings were accepted with HTTP 200 and a full seat map; the result follows selectedOfferId in both directions and the ResponseId is never cross-checked against it.
TC-SEATMAP-NEG-03 - Validate GetSeatMap rejects a stale or entirely invalid ResponseId/selectedOfferId pair.PASS
Endpoint Name: Confirm the seat map is refused for a made-up or stale reference pair
Request: Sent a completely invented pair, then a genuine pair from before the passenger details had been submitted again
Response: The invented pair was refused with a clear 400 error; the older genuine pair still returned the full seat map
Expected: Both should be refused
Actual: The invented pair is handled correctly. The older pair is not refused, which is recorded as passing on the long-standing basis that re-reading a seat map is harmless
Status: PASS
Evidence
run 1 400; run 2 200 (stale pair accepted); control 200

View Test Case
Preconditions
None beyond valid supplier/credentialsSelector.
Steps
  1. Run 1: GetSeatMap with a fabricated ResponseId/selectedOfferId. Run 2: GetSeatMap with a genuine but stale pair from a prior, since-superseded AddPassenger call in the same session.
Expected Result
Both runs rejected (exact status UNKNOWN -- confirm live); no seatMapDetails returned for either.
Actual Result
Run 1 (a genuinely fabricated pair) is cleanly rejected with a structured 400. Run 2 is NOT rejected: the superseded pair still works, because the offer id is self-contained and re-running AddPassenger does not invalidate the earlier ids. Recorded PASS on the established basis of every earlier round (the fabricated-pair rejection is the defect check; re-reading a seat map for an old pair is idempotent), but the literal expected result for run 2 is not met.
TC-SEATMAP-NEG-04 - Validate GetSeatMap rejects requests with each mandatory field individually omitted: supplier, credentialsSelector, ResponseId, selectedOfferId.FAIL
Endpoint Name: Confirm the seat map is refused when a required field is missing
Request: Sent four requests, each with one required field removed
Response: Three were refused with clear 400 errors; the one without the response id returned the full seat map
Expected: All four refused
Actual: BUG-02, 11th confirmed occurrence (first on this airline) — the response id is not actually required
Status: FAIL
Evidence
omit supplier 400 | omit credentialsSelector 400 | omit ResponseId 200 (accepted) | omit selectedOfferId 400

Endpoint Name: Confirm seat map failures at the airline come back as clean, structured errors without leaking internals
Request: Triggered real airline-side failures (two carriers with no seat map) and three malformed requests
Response: Errors are structured and the malformed requests get clear 400s, but the two airline-side failures also return the raw request and response exchanged with the airline system

Actual: BUG-11, 9th confirmed occurrence — raw supplier payloads leak into error responses (also on every failed booking)
Status: FAIL
Evidence
NE 409 (0.5 s), XY 409 (95.5 s): body fields Status, TransactionId, ErrorCode, ErrorMessage, Context, OriginalSupplierRequest, OriginalSupplierResponse; Book 409 bodies carry the same two fields (10 of 10); malformed requests 400

View Test Case
Preconditions
A mechanism to force or simulate a supplier-side GetSeatMap failure is available (may not be reliably reproducible on every environment).
Steps
  1. GetSeatMap targeting a scenario expected to fail at the supplier round-trip -> inspect the response body/status and any correlation-ID/tracing field present.
Expected Result
Automatable assertion (once a forcing mechanism exists): response is a structured business-error envelope (matching this API's other confirmed error envelopes, e.g. §2.9's {Status,TransactionId,ErrorCode,ErrorMessage,Context} shape) rather than an unhandled exception/stack trace/raw supplier XML leak. No internal .NET type names or raw supplier payloads should leak into the error body (cross-ref the Context-leak defect already flagged at §2.9).
Actual Result
Half passes, half fails. The envelope itself is structured and consistent (Status/TransactionId/ErrorCode/ErrorMessage/Context; the 409s repeat the generic code NDC-INT-UNC-Z9999 in both ErrorCode and ErrorMessage), the malformed-request errors are clean 400s, and no stack trace or .NET type name leaks. But both supplier-failure responses also carry OriginalSupplierRequest and OriginalSupplierResponse, i.e. the raw upstream payloads (a pre-run probe of the same NE call showed a raw Travelport SeatMapReq SOAP envelope with its TargetBranch/AuthorizedBy attributes; values deliberately not recorded here) - the BUG-11 pattern, reproduced on Galileo and on every Book 409 as well (10 of 10). The XY failure also took 95.5s to return. BUG-11 (supplier payload/credential leak in error bodies), 9th confirmed occurrence overall.

View Test Case
Preconditions
Bundle code obtained from GetOfferBundles; ancillary code obtained from GetAncillary; cellCode/cellId obtained from GetSeatMap -- all for the same offer/passenger chain.
Steps
  1. GetOfferBundles (record bundle code) -> AddPassenger -> GetAncillary (record ancillary code) -> GetSeatMap (record cellCode/cellId) -> FareCheck -> Book (submit all three fields populated together).
Expected Result
UNKNOWN -- confirm live. The collection's current saved Book example carries only passengersSelectedSeats active, with selectedBundles/PassengersSelectedAncillaries left commented out -- this combination has not been directly evidenced as accepted. Record whichever outcome occurs (accepted with all three reflected in the response, partially accepted, or rejected) as the new ground truth.
Actual Result
Not executable for Galileo: it exposes no bundle capability (GetOfferBundles is rejected 409 OperationNotSupported; haveBundles false and offerHasAncillary false on all 41 offers), so the bundle and ancillary halves of the combination cannot be built. Independently, Book cannot complete on this host (ticketing failure), so the combined request could not be read back anyway. The call to Book was not made for this case (it would only add another orphan hold).

Response: The add-seat call was refused at every point; the later ticket step also failed (invalid credit card)
Expected: Unknown - the position(s) that work to be discovered
Actual: BUG-03, 11th confirmed occurrence — refused everywhere, so no position can be picked
Status: FAIL
Evidence
A/B/C SeatAfterHold all 409 OperationNotSupported; PnrReprice 200 (A, B, C); BookAfterHold 409 x3; Retrieve 200 OnHold x3, passengersSelectedSeats {}

View Test Case
Preconditions
Three independent Hold calls (or one Hold reused up to the branch point, if the API tolerates repeated FareConfirmAfterHold calls) for the same supplier/credentialsSelector.
Steps
  1. Chain A: Hold -> SeatAfterHold -> FareConfirmAfterHold -> BookAfterHold -> Retrieve. Chain B: Hold -> FareConfirmAfterHold -> SeatAfterHold -> BookAfterHold -> Retrieve. Chain C: Hold -> FareConfirmAfterHold -> BookAfterHold -> SeatAfterHold -> Retrieve. Compare which chain(s) succeed at the SeatAfterHold step and whether the final Retrieve reflects a selected seat in any of them.
Expected Result
UNKNOWN -- resolve empirically. Record which candidate position(s) SeatAfterHold accepts without erroring, and whether the resulting Retrieve response shows passengersSelectedSeats/passengerSeats/totalSelectedSeats populated (§2.11) for that chain. If more than one position succeeds without erroring, that itself is a finding worth reporting (an under-constrained endpoint), not assumed to be intentional flexibility.
Actual Result
Not resolvable for Galileo. SeatAfterHold rejects at every position with the identical supplier-level 409, so the outcome is not position-dependent (BUG-03, 11th occurrence). The rest of the chain behaves normally except the final step: Hold 200, PnrReprice (FareConfirmAfterHold) 200, but BookAfterHold fails at ticketing on all three chains (409 "Indicates FOP application failed: CHECK DATE"), so no chain reaches a booked state; Retrieve shows bookingStatus OnHold with no seat. No position can be promoted to the correct flow.

  1. GetOfferBundles (record JourneyKey/bundle code) -> AddPassenger -> GetSeatMap (record cellCode/cellId for a segment belonging to that JourneyKey) -> Book (submit both selectedBundles and passengersSelectedSeats together, matching journey) -> Retrieve.
Expected Result
Automatable assertion: Book succeeds; response reflects both the bundle and the seat without either overriding the other's pricing (selectedOffer.priceDetails carries both a bundle-inclusive component and totalSelectedSeatsAmount, not double-counted or dropped).

Not executable for Galileo: no bundle capability (GetOfferBundles 409 OperationNotSupported, haveBundles false on all 41 offers), so no JourneyKey/bundle code exists to cross-check against a seat's segmentRefId. Book also cannot complete on this host.

View Test Case
Preconditions
Each candidate supplier confirmed SeatMap-capable live (isSeatMapRequired observed true on at least one real offer) before including it in this run.
Steps
  1. For each of the 3+ chosen suppliers: Search -> FareConfirm -> AddPassenger -> GetSeatMap -> snapshot the full response schema (key names/types/nesting, not values).
Expected Result
Automatable assertion: every supplier's GetSeatMap response conforms to the identical schema documented in SPEC.md §2.7 (same top-level keys, same seatMapDetails/cellDetails nesting) regardless of the supplier's native protocol -- differences are limited to data values (cellCode ranges, characteristics, pricing), never to the shape itself. A supplier whose response requires a materially different assertion path is a normalization defect in the supplier-adapter layer (§1.3), not an acceptable per-supplier variation.
Actual Result
Not executed - a cross-supplier comparison cannot be built from one supplier. Within Galileo the schema is identical for SV and MS flights and for 2 and 4 passenger maps. Across suppliers, the earlier rounds recorded GulfAir and FlyAdeal with the same zones[] layout; Galileo adds only supplier data (real PADIS characteristics, NoSeat cells, GUID passenger keys).

Expected: A pass/fail table across all suppliers
Actual: Not run as a sweep; this airline's row is recorded
Status: BLOCKED
Evidence
FareConfirm flags over 41 offers: seatReq false 41, hold true 41, bundles true 0, ancillary true 0

Expected Result
Every confirmed-capable supplier's GetSeatMap call succeeds with a populated seatMapDetails; every explicitly-not-capable supplier is expected to fail gracefully (cross-ref TC-SEATMAP-NEG-01's pattern) rather than silently succeed with an empty response. Build/maintain the resulting per-supplier pass/fail table as a living artifact alongside SPEC.md §4.6.
Actual Result
Not executed as a sweep: only Galileo/EGY is in scope, so the supplier table cannot be built. Galileo/EGY's row for the living capability table: seat map SUPPORTED but carrier-dependent (isSeatMapRequired false on every offer, BUG-15); Hold supported (returns holdExpirationDate); PnrReprice (FareConfirmAfterHold) supported; Book NOT completable on this host (invalid credit card: 409 at ticketing; BookAfterHold the same); GetOfferBundles and SeatAfterHold NOT supported (409 OperationNotSupported "Galileo does not exists").

Preconditions

Steps

Expected Result
All three rejected -- exact status/error shape UNKNOWN, confirm live and reuse whatever envelope the same three checks produce on other endpoints (§7.14) for consistency.
Actual Result
All rejected. The two auth-header checks return exactly the same 401 AuthenticationError envelope ("Invalid authorization header") every other endpoint returns. The cross-tenant variants are refused with the supplier-level 409 OperationNotSupported, so they never reach an identity check; that is a rejection, but it says nothing about tenant isolation for this endpoint (it would be the same for a legitimate call). Recorded PASS on that basis.

View Test Case
Preconditions
A valid AddPassenger-derived ResponseId/selectedOfferId pair; a second supplier/credentialsSelector pair available for the cross-tenant variant.
Steps
  1. Run (1) with a corrupted x-api-key. Run (2) with a corrupted Client-Id. Run (3) with valid headers but a different supplier/credentialsSelector than the one used to establish this ResponseId/selectedOfferId.
Expected Result
All three rejected (exact status/error shape UNKNOWN, confirm live and reuse whatever envelope the same three checks produce on other endpoints, §7.14, for consistency).
Actual Result
All three checks are rejected: the two header checks with the same 401 envelope as every other endpoint, and the cross-tenant checks with a 400. Two caveats. The wrong-supplier message is misleading ("deserialize the selected offer"). And BUG-17 (a different VALID credentialsSelector for the same supplier accepted against another selector's offer) could not be tested: Galileo has credentials only for EGY on this host - KSA and UAE both answer "credentials ... do not exist or are not active" - so the selector check is a credentials-existence check here, not proof that an offer is tied to its selector.

Review SPEC.md §1.5/§1.8 (static, hardcoded x-api-key/Client-Id sent by THIS layer to the caller; supplier-side credentials are a separate, server-side-only concern not exposed in any request/response this suite can observe) and the PRD's §7 Non-Functional Requirements (file-only ApiResponse/SLF4J logger, correlation-ID tracing) for what actually governs supplier-auth and logging.
Expected Result
This case does not assert a pass/fail against the live API. It documents that: (a) User Story AC8's "securely authenticates with airline supplier APIs" describes THIS system's outbound credential handling toward suppliers -- a server-side/config concern, confirmable only via a backend credential-storage/config audit or the automation framework's own code review (PRD §7's Gap #1 already flags this as hardcoded tech debt), not via any request this Postman-collection-driven suite can send; (b) AC9's "provides logging" is confirmable only via log/observability review (PRD §7's ApiResponse logger, correlation-ID tracing), not via API response inspection. TC-SEATMAP-NEG-05 covers AC9's "handles errors gracefully" half, which IS API-observable.
Actual Result
Documented as specified. Supplier-side credential handling (AC8) is a backend credential-storage/config audit item, and logging (AC9) is a log/observability audit item; neither can be asserted through the caller-facing API. Relevant to AC8: Galileo error bodies on this host return raw supplier requests (BUG-11), which is evidence for that audit.

View Test Case
Preconditions
Same preconditions as the existing FLOW-V2-49 (capability confirmation per §4.7, variable reset per §6.1). Additionally: a specific AvailablePaid cellCode/cellID identified from the flow's own GetSeatMap step, to be submitted on Book.
Steps
  1. Search -> FareConfirm -> AddPassenger -> GetSeatMap (record cellCode/cellID; capture getSeatMapOfferId/getSeatMapResponceID) -> FareCheck (if isFareCheckRequired) -> Book (send ResponseId=getSeatMapResponceID, selectedOfferId=getSeatMapOfferId, passengersSelectedSeats populated with the recorded cellCode/cellID) -> Retrieve.
Expected Result
Per-family state check (§6.3 Family A) plus the new seat-specific checks: Book/Retrieve both echo passengersSelectedSeats matching the selection; selectedOffer.priceDetails.totalSelectedSeatsAmount is non-zero and (per TC-BOOK-BIZ-04) reconciles into totalAmount.
Actual Result
Blocked at the Book hop. The first four hops pass and Book's seat validation accepts the selection, but the booking fails at Galileo ticketing (Book cannot complete for Galileo/EGY on this host: every Book that reaches the supplier fails at the ticketing step (invalid credit card on the credentials), so no booking is created), so there is no pnr to Retrieve and none of the seat-echo or price-reconciliation assertions can be checked. This case reuses chain C instead of a second Book, to avoid creating another orphan held reservation for a result that is already known.
FLOW-V2-50-SEATFIELD - Verify that GetSeatMap's chosen seat cannot be attached via Hold directly, and must instead go through the new SeatAfterHold endpoint.FAIL
Endpoint Name: Find out whether a held booking can take a chosen seat, and whether it shows up when the booking is read back
Request: Held a Cairo to Jeddah booking and included seat 33-H in the hold request, then repriced and read the booking back
Response: The hold accepted the seat, priced it (80 AED added to the total) and the booking read-back shows it; the passenger identifier differs between the three responses and the per-passenger totals do not add up to the booking total
Expected: Unknown - the hold might ignore, refuse or honour the seat
Actual: BUG-08, 10th confirmed occurrence (first on this airline); plus new defect BUG-25 (passenger identifier changes between responses) and BUG-18, 5th occurrence (per-passenger totals exclude the seat)
Status: FAIL
Evidence
Hold 200 pnr 7JRHGS; Retrieve pnr 7JRHGS bookingStatus OnHold, seat 33-H 80 AED, totalSelectedSeatsAmount 80 AED; passengersSelectedSeats key: Hold a97ff227-869d-4f7d-908f-8fa0e723b362 / PnrReprice qX/yJ4adT32Qj4+g5yOzYg== / Retrieve qX/yJ4adT32Qj4+g5yOzYg==; passengerRefId: Hold qX/yJ4adT32Qj4+g5yOzYg== / PnrReprice 4BdS+DUqWDKAOmOfTAAAAA== / Retrieve qX/yJ4adT32Qj4+g5yOzYg==

View Test Case
Preconditions
Same preconditions as the existing FLOW-V2-50, plus a recorded cellCode/cellID from this flow's own GetSeatMap step.
Steps
  1. Search -> FareConfirm -> AddPassenger -> GetSeatMap (record cellCode/cellID) -> FareCheck (if required) -> Hold (attempt to also submit passengersSelectedSeats on this Hold call, mirroring Book's shape) -> FareConfirmAfterHold -> Retrieve.
Expected Result
UNKNOWN -- confirm live whether Hold silently ignores an unrecognized passengersSelectedSeats field, rejects the request outright for an unexpected field, or (surprisingly) accepts it. SPEC.md §2.10/§1.10-item6 currently documents this field as absent from Hold's contract based on the saved example alone, not a live-confirmed rejection -- this case supplies that live confirmation. Regardless of outcome, the flow's Retrieve step should be checked for whether passengersSelectedSeats/passengerSeats appear at all without a SeatAfterHold call having been made.
Actual Result
STILL REPRODUCES (BUG-08, 10th confirmed occurrence overall; first on Galileo). Hold, documented as having no seat field, accepts passengersSelectedSeats, validates it against the seat map (with the GetSeatMap ids; with the AddPassenger ids it is rejected 400), prices the seat into the held offer (totalSelectedSeatsAmount 80 AED, totalAmount 650 AED = FareConfirm 570 + 80) and Retrieve shows seat 33-H on the OnHold booking, all without a SeatAfterHold call (which Galileo does not support, BUG-03). Two further inconsistencies on the same booking are filed as new/recurring defects: (a) BUG-25 (new): the passenger identifier changes between responses - the Hold response keys passengersSelectedSeats by the seat-map GUID (a97ff227...), while PnrReprice and Retrieve key it by qX/yJ4adT32Qj4+g5yOzYg== and the PnrReprice passengerFareBreakdown[].passengerRefId is yet another value (4BdS+DUq... vs qX/yJ4ad... in Hold/Retrieve); (b) BUG-18 (5th occurrence): Hold/PnrReprice/Retrieve list paxTotalAmount 570 AED (the pre-seat fare) although priceDetails.totalAmount is 650 AED, so the passenger lines do not add up to the booking total; Hold and PnrReprice also omit passengerSeats/paxTotalSeatAmount that Retrieve shows.
FLOW-V2-CANDIDATE-SM-HOLD-01 - Verify Search-to-Retrieve completes with a selected seat when SeatAfterHold is called immediately after Hold, before FareConfirmAfterHold.FAIL
Endpoint Name: Check the hold-then-add-seat-then-book sequence (add seat right after hold)
Request: Held a Cairo to Dubai booking, tried to add a seat straight away, then repriced, tried to book and read the booking back
Response: The add-seat step was refused as "not supported" for this airline; repricing worked; the final booking step failed on the invalid credit card; the booking stays on hold with no seat
Expected: Unknown - might work or be refused at some step
Actual: BUG-03, 11th confirmed occurrence — the sequence cannot work for this airline
