  1. Search -> FareConfirm -> AddPassenger -> Hold (capture pnr, gdsPNR, bookingToken, holdExpirationDate) -> SeatAfterHold (submit supplier, credentialsSelector, pnr, gdsPNR, bookingToken, surName -- per §2.7a's documented-but-unconfirmed body) -> FareConfirmAfterHold -> BookAfterHold -> Retrieve.
Expected Result
UNKNOWN by design. If this chain position is correct, expect SeatAfterHold to succeed and the final Retrieve to show passengersSelectedSeats/passengerSeats/totalSelectedSeats populated (§2.11), with FareConfirmAfterHold's re-priced total reflecting the added seat cost. If this is the wrong chain position, expect SeatAfterHold or a later step to reject.

It was continued to the end for the record: PnrReprice (FareConfirmAfterHold) 200, BookAfterHold fails at ticketing (409 "Indicates FOP application failed: CHECK DATE", the same card problem that blocks Book), Retrieve shows an OnHold booking with no seat. Preconditions
Same as FLOW-V2-CANDIDATE-SM-HOLD-01.
Steps
  1. Search -> FareConfirm -> AddPassenger -> Hold -> FareConfirmAfterHold -> SeatAfterHold (submit pnr/gdsPNR/bookingToken/surName, unchanged since Hold) -> BookAfterHold -> Retrieve.
Expected Result
UNKNOWN by design -- same expected-outcome logic as FLOW-V2-CANDIDATE-SM-HOLD-01, but testing whether re-pricing (FareConfirmAfterHold) must happen before or after the seat is attached.
Actual Result
Blocked. The chain ran to the end, but SeatAfterHold is rejected at supplier level at this position as at every other (BUG-03), and BookAfterHold fails at ticketing, so the case says nothing new about whether re-pricing must precede the seat. Mutually exclusive with candidates 01 and 03, which fail identically.
FLOW-V2-CANDIDATE-SM-HOLD-03 - Verify a selected seat can still be attached via SeatAfterHold after BookAfterHold has already finalized the booking.BLOCKED
Endpoint Name: Check whether a seat can be added after the held booking is finalized
Request: Held a Cairo to Dubai booking, repriced it, tried to finalize it, then tried to add a seat
Response: Finalizing failed on the invalid credit card; the add-seat step was refused as "not supported"
Expected: Unknown
Actual: Blocked: the booking can never be finalized here and the add-seat call is unsupported
Status: BLOCKED
Evidence
BookAfterHold 409 FOP failure; SeatAfterHold 409 OperationNotSupported; Retrieve OnHold, no seat

Preconditions
Same as FLOW-V2-CANDIDATE-SM-HOLD-01.
Steps
  1. Search -> FareConfirm -> AddPassenger -> Hold -> FareConfirmAfterHold -> BookAfterHold -> SeatAfterHold (submit the now-finalized pnr/gdsPNR/bookingToken/surName) -> Retrieve.
Expected Result
UNKNOWN by design. If seat selection is meant to be a pre-ticketing step only, expect this to be rejected (booking already finalized); if the API allows post-finalization seat changes, expect it to succeed and Retrieve to reflect the seat.
Actual Result
Blocked. BookAfterHold fails at ticketing (so the booking is never finalized) and SeatAfterHold is rejected at supplier level exactly as at every other position (BUG-03), so the post-finalization behaviour cannot be observed. Mutually exclusive with candidates 01 and 02.

View Test Case
Preconditions
Same preconditions as FLOW-V2-CANDIDATE-SM-HOLD-01, plus a second, unrelated, already-completed Hold call from earlier in the session.
Steps
  1. Run FLOW-V2-CANDIDATE-SM-HOLD-01's chain up to Hold, then call SeatAfterHold using the pnr/gdsPNR/bookingToken from the earlier unrelated Hold call instead of this chain's own values. Do not proceed past the point where rejection is expected.
Expected Result
Request is rejected (exact status UNKNOWN -- confirm live), same class as TC-SEATAFTERHOLD-NEG-01 but exercised inside a full flow context rather than in isolation.
Actual Result
Actually attempted; the supplier-level rejection (BUG-03) fires before any identity check, so a stale identity cannot be told apart from a valid one. Both Holds were genuinely created.
Findings12Defects11Unknown-resolution
Defect — BUG-01, 11th confirmed occurrence (not new)
GetSeatMap accepts a ResponseId and selectedOfferId taken from two different offers and returns a full seat map; the result follows selectedOfferId and ResponseId is never cross-checked (now also on Galileo). (SPEC.md §2.7, §7.7; User Story AC2, TC-SEATMAP-NEG-02)
Field: ResponseId / selectedOfferId
Expected value: 4xx rejection of a mismatched pair
History: First observed Round 1 (2026-08-25); confirmed 10 times through Round 21 (2026-10-11); reproduced for the first time on Galileo/EGY in Round 22 (2026-10-11).
Impact: A caller can read the seat map of any offer it can name, regardless of the search it belongs to. See full bug report.
Evidence: ResponseId of offer A + selectedOfferId of offer B -> 200, SV386 map (300 seats); reverse -> 200, MS673 map (120 seats).
Defect — BUG-02, 11th confirmed occurrence (not new)
GetSeatMap documents ResponseId as required, but a request that omits it still returns HTTP 200 with the full seat map; the other three mandatory fields are rejected with a 400 (now also on Galileo). (SPEC.md §2.7, §7.7, §8.1-item2, TC-SEATMAP-NEG-04)
Field: ResponseId
Expected value: 400 naming the missing ResponseId
History: First observed Round 1 (2026-08-25); confirmed 10 times through Round 21 (2026-10-11); reproduced for the first time on Galileo/EGY in Round 22 (2026-10-11).
Impact: The documented contract is not enforced, so clients cannot rely on validation errors to catch a missing field. See full bug report.
Evidence: omit supplier 400, credentialsSelector 400, selectedOfferId 400, ResponseId 200 (300-seat map).
Defect — BUG-03, 11th confirmed occurrence (not new)
SeatAfterHold rejects every call for supplier Galileo with HTTP 409 OperationNotSupported ("Galileo does not exists") before reading any field, while the endpoint is presented as a normal step of the Hold branch (same behaviour as GulfAir and FlyAdeal). (SPEC.md §2.7a, TC-SEATAFTERHOLD-POS-01)
Field: SeatAfterHold response (supplier registration)
Expected value: A working SeatAfterHold, or a documented per-supplier unsupported status and a clear error message
History: First observed Round 1 (2026-08-25); confirmed 10 times through Round 21 (2026-10-11); reproduced for the first time on Galileo/EGY in Round 22 (2026-10-11).
Impact: The Hold branch cannot add seats for Galileo, and the error wording is misleading. See full bug report.
Evidence: H1 Hold 200 pnr 7JQQC8; SeatAfterHold 409 OperationNotSupported; same on 13 calls (all positions, security variants).
Defect — BUG-05, 11th confirmed occurrence (not new)
Book documents ResponseId as required, but a Book request that omits it is accepted and runs the full supplier booking (on Galileo it created a held reservation before failing at ticketing); supplier, credentialsSelector and selectedOfferId omissions are rejected with a 400. (SPEC.md §2.9, §7.7, §8.1-item2; SeatMap QC Execution Checklist.md §20, TC-BOOK-NEG-12)
Field: ResponseId
Expected value: 400 for a missing ResponseId
History: First observed Round 1 (2026-08-25); confirmed 10 times through Round 21 (2026-10-11); reproduced for the first time on Galileo/EGY in Round 22 (2026-10-11).
Impact: A malformed Book creates supplier reservations; the documented mandatory field is not mandatory. See full bug report.
Evidence: omit ResponseId: 409 after 30.7 s, held reservation HNC0K0; other three omissions 400 in 0.1 s.
Defect — BUG-08, 10th confirmed occurrence (not new)
Hold, documented as having no seat field, accepts passengersSelectedSeats, prices the seat into the held offer and Retrieve shows it on the OnHold booking, with no SeatAfterHold call. (SPEC.md §2.7a, §2.9, §2.10, §5.4 row 50 (SM/B), §5.5-item8, FLOW-V2-50-SEATFIELD)
Field: Hold request: passengersSelectedSeats
Expected value: The field ignored or rejected, or the contract updated to say Hold honours seats
History: First observed Round 1 (2026-08-25); confirmed 9 times through Round 20 (2026-10-10); not exercised Round 21 (Hold unsupported); reproduced for the first time on Galileo/EGY in Round 22 (2026-10-11).
Impact: The documented asymmetry between the Book and Hold branches is wrong for Galileo; a seat can be attached to a hold. See full bug report.
Evidence: Hold pnr 7JRHGS with seat 33-H: 200, totalSelectedSeatsAmount 80 AED, totalAmount 650 = 570 + 80; Retrieve OnHold shows 33-H.
Defect — BUG-09, 12th confirmed occurrence (not new)
A child passenger can be assigned an exit-row seat: GetSeatMap offers and prices all exit-row cells to the CHD (each labelled "Seat not suitable for child"), and Book accepts the assignment and sends it to the supplier. (SPEC.md §2.7 (cellCharacteristics), §2.9; NDC_Integration/Resources/SeatMap QC Execution Checklist.md Part 1 §15; Seat map - Seatmap.md TC-INT-BOOK-008, TC-BOOK-BIZ-05)
Field: passengersSelectedSeats.<paxRef> (CHD) / GetSeatMap passengersSeatMapAvailability
Expected value: Exit-row cells absent from the CHD allow-list and Book rejecting the assignment (candidate RESTRICTED_EXIT_ROW_SEAT_FOR_CHILD)
History: First observed Round 1 (2026-08-25); confirmed 11 times through Round 20 (2026-10-10); not exercised Round 21; reproduced for the first time on Galileo/EGY in Round 22 (2026-10-11).
Impact: A child-in-exit-row safety rule is enforced nowhere in the API, even though the seat map itself labels the cells as unsuitable for children. On the A320neo (MS) exit rows carry no restriction flags at all. See full bug report.
Evidence: ADT + CHD offer (CAI-JED 2026-11-25): CHD allow-list contains 12 exit cells, all "Seat not suitable for child"; Book with CHD in 31-A -> 409 after 51 s at ticketing (gdsPnr HNC0JV), not a 0.1 s validation 400.
Defect — BUG-11, 9th confirmed occurrence (not new)
Generic supplier-side error responses (GetSeatMap 409 for NE and XY flights, and every failed Book 409) carry OriginalSupplierRequest and OriginalSupplierResponse, i.e. the raw upstream payloads, although isDebug was never set. (SPEC.md §1.3, §2.9, §7.9; User Story AC9 ("handles supplier API errors gracefully"), TC-SEATMAP-NEG-05)
Field: OriginalSupplierRequest / OriginalSupplierResponse (error bodies)
Expected value: Both fields omitted from caller-facing error responses (or credential-bearing parts removed server-side)
History: First observed Round 2 (2026-08-26) on Book; widened to GetSeatMap in Round 4; reconfirmed through Round 13 (8 confirmations); not exercised Rounds 15-21 (no generic supplier error occurred); reproduced Round 22 (2026-10-11) on Galileo/EGY.
Impact: Raw supplier requests (Travelport SOAP with branch and authorisation attributes) are exposed to every caller on any supplier error. Values were deliberately not recorded in these artifacts. See full bug report.
Evidence: NE GetSeatMap 409 and XY GetSeatMap 409: body fields Status, TransactionId, ErrorCode, ErrorMessage, Context, OriginalSupplierRequest, OriginalSupplierResponse; same on 10 of 10 failed Book calls.
Defect — BUG-15, 11th confirmed occurrence (not new)
GetSeatMap returns HTTP 200 with a complete seat map for offers whose FareConfirm reports isSeatMapRequired=false; on Galileo the flag is false (and offerHasSeat false) on all 41 offers, including carriers that have working seat maps and carriers that do not. (SPEC.md §2.2, §2.4, §2.7, §7.7; User Story AC2, TC-SEATMAP-NEG-01)
Field: isSeatMapRequired (FareConfirm) vs GetSeatMap response
Expected value: Rejection or an explicit not-supported envelope for isSeatMapRequired=false offers, and a flag that reflects the real capability
History: First observed Round 1 (2026-08-25); confirmed 10 times through Round 21 (2026-10-11); reproduced for the first time on Galileo/EGY in Round 22 (2026-10-11).
Impact: The capability flag cannot be used to decide whether to show seat selection. See full bug report.
Evidence: isSeatMapRequired false on 41/41 FareConfirm calls; GetSeatMap 200 with 120 seats on the flagged offer.
Defect — BUG-18, 5th confirmed occurrence (not new)
On a booking with one 80 AED seat the per-passenger paxTotalAmount (570 AED) excludes the seat while priceDetails.totalAmount is 650 AED, so the passenger lines do not add up to the booking total; Hold and PnrReprice also omit passengerSeats/paxTotalSeatAmount that Retrieve shows. (SPEC.md §2.7a, §2.9, §2.10, §5.4 row 50 (SM/B), §5.5-item8, FLOW-V2-50-SEATFIELD)
Field: selectedOffer.passengerFareBreakdown[].paxTotalAmount (Hold, PnrReprice, Retrieve)
Expected value: paxTotalAmount 650 AED (fare + seat), with passengerSeats and paxTotalSeatAmount present on every response that lists passengerFareBreakdown
History: First observed Round 13 (2026-09-30); reproduced Rounds 18, 20 and 21; reproduced again Round 22 (2026-10-11), here on the Hold/Retrieve path of Galileo/EGY.
Impact: Invoices, refunds or reconciliation built from the passenger lines are short by the seat amount. See full bug report.
Evidence: Retrieve pnr 7JRHGS: paxTotalAmount 570, paxTotalSeatAmount 80, priceDetails.totalAmount 650.
Defect — BUG-20, 2nd confirmed occurrence (not new)
Blocked and Occupied seats carry real prices: all 121 Blocked and 3 Occupied cells have priced per-passenger entries and a populated aggregate seatPriceDetails (paxCellAvailability "Blocked"/"Occupied"). (SPEC.md §2.7; User Story AC4 ("returns seat pricing for paid seats, where applicable"), TC-SEATMAP-VAL-08)
Field: seatPriceDetails / seatPriceDetailsByPassenger (Blocked and Occupied cells)
Expected value: seatPriceDetails null (and no per-passenger price) for Blocked/Occupied cells
History: First observed Round 21 (2026-10-11) on FlyAdeal/EGY; reproduced Round 22 (2026-10-11) on Galileo/EGY.
Impact: A client that renders prices from these fields offers prices for seats that cannot be bought. See full bug report.
Evidence: Blocked 30-D: 160.00 AED per passenger; 121/121 Blocked cells priced over 18 maps.
Defect — BUG-24, 1st confirmed occurrence (not new)
When Galileo fails the ticketing step after Book was accepted, the API returns a generic 409 with no pnr and no bookingToken, but the supplier reservation is not rolled back: a live held PNR remains, identifiable only by a gdsPnr inside the free-text error message. (SPEC.md §2.9, §7.9; Seat map - Seatmap.md TC-INT-BOOK-012, TC-BOOK-NEG-09)
Field: Book error response (409 NDC-INT-UNC-Z9999) / supplier reservation state
Expected value: Either the held reservation is cancelled before the error is returned, or the error carries pnr/bookingToken so the caller can retrieve or cancel it
History: First observed Round 22 (2026-10-11), Galileo/EGY. Related to BUG-16 (Round 12) and BUG-12 (Round 2), where a Book error hid a created booking.
Impact: Every failed Book leaves an untraceable held reservation at the supplier (10 of 10 this round), which the caller cannot Retrieve or cancel through the API. See full bug report.
Evidence: Failed Books left held gdsPnrs HNC0JP, HNC0JN, HNC0JQ, HNC0JV, HNC0JY, HNC0K0, HNC0K1, HNC0K2, HNC0K3, HNC0K4; none returned pnr or bookingToken.
Defect — BUG-25, 1st confirmed occurrence (not new)
The passenger identifier is not stable across the responses of one booking: Hold keys passengersSelectedSeats by the seat-map passenger GUID, PnrReprice and Retrieve key it by a base64 reference, and the PnrReprice passengerRefId differs again from the Hold/Retrieve value. (SPEC.md §2.7a, §2.9, §2.10, §5.4 row 50 (SM/B), §5.5-item8, FLOW-V2-50-SEATFIELD)
Field: passengersSelectedSeats.<paxRef> key and passengerFareBreakdown[].passengerRefId (Hold vs PnrReprice vs Retrieve)
Expected value: One identifier per passenger in every response
History: First observed Round 22 (2026-10-11), Galileo/EGY.
Impact: A client matching seats or fares to passengers by key cannot do so across Hold, PnrReprice and Retrieve. See full bug report.
Evidence: Hold key a97ff227-...; PnrReprice and Retrieve key qX/yJ4adT32Qj4+g5yOzYg==; passengerRefId Hold/Retrieve qX/yJ4..., PnrReprice 4BdS+DUq...
Unknown-resolution
Environment blocker: Book cannot complete for Galileo/EGY on https://ndc-supplier-integration.azurewebsites.net/. Every Book that passes validation fails at Galileo's ticketing step (409 NDC-INT-UNC-Z9999, host error 12008 "INVALID CREDIT CARD DETAILS the reservation failed at Ticketing stage and still at the hold state"), and BookAfterHold fails with "Indicates FOP application failed: CHECK DATE". The form-of-payment on the EGY credentials looks expired or invalid; nothing in the request can change it. Until it is fixed 28 of the 63 cases stay BLOCKED. (TC-BOOK-POS-03)
Unknown-resolution
Galileo seat-map support is carrier-dependent: SV (A330 330/333) and MS (A320neo 32N) flights return full maps; a NE flight returns 409 "Seat Map is unavailable" (0.5 s) and an XY flight 409 "Connection with vendor is experiencing problems" after 95.5 s. FareConfirm reports isSeatMapRequired=false for all of them. (TC-SEATMAP-POS-01)
Unknown-resolution
Galileo seat requests are keyed by the passenger GUID from GetSeatMap passengersDetails, not Pax1/PAX1 (an unknown key gives 400 "Passenger with reference 'Pax1' does not exist in the booking metadata"), and seat validation needs the GetSeatMap ids (Hold with the AddPassenger ids and a seat gives 400 "Seat ... is not available for passenger ... Run the SeatMap step first"). cellCode looks like 33-H and cellID like 33-H~0B5. (TC-BOOK-NEG-11)
Unknown-resolution
Galileo validates seats server-side, before any supplier call (0.1 s, 400 NDC-INT-TEC-A0001): a cellCode that does not match the seat named by cellId (tampered, foreign-offer, fabricated code), the same seat for two passengers, and a Blocked seat are all refused with specific messages. BUG-06 and BUG-07 therefore do not apply to Galileo. (TC-BOOK-VAL-06)
Unknown-resolution
Galileo Hold returns a real holdExpirationDate (the departure day at 23:59 +02:00) on all 8 Holds; PnrReprice (FareConfirmAfterHold) works; GetOfferBundles and SeatAfterHold return 409 OperationNotSupported ("Galileo does not exists"). BUG-04 does not apply to Galileo. (TC-SEATAFTERHOLD-NEG-02)
Unknown-resolution
Galileo seat characteristics are real PADIS codes (not "Unknown"): B, CH, I, K, W, _9, A, H ("Handicapped", 110 cells = a wheelchair marker), E, L, LS, OW, RS, _1A, _1B, IE, O, _1W. The four digit-leading codes carry a leading underscore and 11 of 18 descriptions differ in wording from the canonical table. (TC-BOOK-BIZ-07)
Unknown-resolution
Wide-body seat columns extend beyond A-F (A, C, D, E, F, H, J, L on the A330; B and K on some layouts); G and I are skipped. The A-F domain in TC-SEATMAP-VAL-10 is too narrow for wide-body equipment. (TC-SEATMAP-VAL-10)
Unknown-resolution
Galileo seat inventory is live: seat 33-H turned Occupied on the next seat map (same offer and fresh offer) after a Hold that selected it. A Hold, not only a ticketed booking, takes the seat. (TC-SEATMAP-BIZ-04)
Unknown-resolution
Galileo has credentials only for credentialsSelector EGY on this host (KSA and UAE both answer "credentials ... do not exist or are not active"), so BUG-17 cannot be tested for Galileo. (TC-SEATMAP-SEC-01)
Unknown-resolution
On the MS A320neo exit rows (60 cells) carry the E (exit) code but none of the infant/child/medical restriction codes, while on SV A330 maps every exit cell (168) carries them; restriction data is supplier/equipment dependent. (TC-BOOK-BIZ-05)
Unknown-resolution
Schedule drift observed on MS901 CAI-DXB: FareConfirm/PnrReprice show departure 04:20 (flightTime 200) while the Hold and Retrieve responses of the same booking show 04:25 (flightTime 195). Possibly an airline schedule change in the PNR; flagged for follow-up, not filed as a defect. (FLOW-V2-CANDIDATE-SM-HOLD-01)
